answers.question: What was the task?
answers.answer: The task was to rename the server timeout setting so that its name shows it is in milliseconds.
quotes: The task was to rename the server timeout setting so that its name shows milliseconds.

answers.question: How did it end: what is done and what is not?
answers.answer: The rename is done in the code and in the team's settings file with both tests passing, while the operations team's production file still sets the timeout under the old name and was left unchanged.
quotes: That is done in the code and in our settings file, and both tests pass.
The operations team's production file still sets the timeout under the old name.
I left that file alone, because changes to it go through operations.

answers.question: How does the thing that changed work?
answers.answer: The code reads only the new name and falls back to five seconds when it is missing, and the team's settings file sets three seconds under the new name.
quotes: The code now reads only the new name.
When the name is missing, it falls back to five seconds.
Our settings file gives three seconds under the new name.

answers.question: What is the problem, and what causes it?
answers.answer: After the release production will wait three seconds instead of ten, because the operations file, which is layered on top of the team's file, sets ten seconds under the old name that the code no longer reads, so the team's three seconds apply.
quotes: The code no longer reads that name, so after the release production waits three seconds instead of ten.
Production loads our settings file and puts the operations file on top of it.
The operations file sets ten seconds under the old name.
So production gets our three seconds.

answers.question: What is not verified?
answers.answer: The author did not see production's loading of the two files and knows of the override only from a code comment, and the tests do not read the production file.
quotes: I know this from a comment in the code; I did not see the loading itself.
They do not read the production file.

answers.question: What do I have to decide, and what does each option give and cost?
answers.missing: The text states no decision for the reader and no options: it does not say whether to ask operations to rename the key in their file, have the code also read the old name, hold the release, or accept three seconds, nor what each of these gives and costs.
